boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Colorado College
boards.description: Late-night dining at Colorado College is defined by a mix of on-campus traditions like Midnight Rasty and a selection of local diners and drive-thrus that cater to students during the intense Block Plan schedule.

cards.title: Midnight Rasty
cards.subtitle: Worner Campus Center
cards.notes: Attend this high-energy campus tradition where students gather for late-night breakfast food like tater tots and donuts during major events.
cards.short_summary: A signature campus event held during high-risk nights like Halloween and Winter Ball, offering free late-night breakfast to the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Rasty is a widely attended campus-sponsored event where Rastall opens late to serve donuts, tater-tots, and pancakes to students.
cards.source_title: Late-Night Oasis: The Life Behind Midnight Rasty - The Catalyst
cards.access_notes: Open late only during specific scheduled 'Midnight Rasty' events throughout the academic year.

cards.title: The C-Store
cards.subtitle: Mathias Hall
cards.notes: Stop by this on-campus convenience store for late-night snacks and essentials, open daily until midnight for student convenience.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus convenience store managed by Bon Appétit that serves as a primary late-night source for groceries and snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Local Goods, commonly known as the C-store, is located in Mathias Hall and is open daily until midnight.
cards.source_title: The C-Store: a Blessing and a Curse - The Catalyst
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 12:00 AM during the academic year.

cards.title: The 24/7 Nevada Stop
cards.subtitle: North Nevada Avenue
cards.notes: Walk to this 24-hour convenience store located just off campus for quick snacks, drinks, and fuel at any hour of the night.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 convenience store located immediately adjacent to the Colorado College campus, serving as a reliable late-night resource.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 825 North Nevada Ave is open 24/7 and provides food, snacks, and drinks.
cards.source_title: 825 North Nevada Ave Colorado Springs CO 80903-4705 - 7-Eleven
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

cards.title: Late-Night Caffeine Fix
cards.subtitle: East Colorado Avenue
cards.notes: Drive through for a late-night Rebel energy drink or coffee, with service available until 11:00 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: A popular drive-thru coffee chain known for its high-energy drinks and late-night operating hours near downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dutch Bros location at 301 E. Colorado Ave is open until 11:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: 301 E. Colorado Ave. - Coffee Shop in Colorado Springs | Dutch Bros Coffee Drive-Thru
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

cards.title: The Calzone Run
cards.subtitle: North Nevada Avenue
cards.notes: Order a custom calzone for late-night delivery or pickup, with the kitchen serving until 1:00 AM most nights.
cards.short_summary: A college-town staple specializing in a wide variety of calzones, offering late-night delivery and pickup services.
cards.evidence_claim: D.P. Dough at 4239 N Nevada Ave is open for pickup and delivery until 1:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: D.P. Dough Delivery Menu | Order Online | 4239 N Nevada Ave Ste 108 Colorado Springs
cards.access_notes: Open for pickup and delivery until 1:00 AM daily.

cards.title: The Big-Ass Slice
cards.subtitle: South Tejon Street
cards.notes: Grab a giant New York-style slice at this downtown spot, which serves its full menu until late in the evening.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza window and restaurant famous for its oversized slices and late-night availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Fat Sully's Pizza at 528 S Tejon St is served every day from 11:00 AM until close, typically late night.
cards.source_title: Fat Sully's | Denver's Best Pizza — Atomic Cowboy
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 12:00 AM or later depending on the night.

cards.title: Post-Game Burger Run
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue
cards.notes: Head to this popular drive-thru for a late-night burger and fries, open until 1:00 AM or later on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A classic West Coast burger chain that has become a popular late-night destination for students since opening in Colorado.
cards.evidence_claim: The In-N-Out at 2895 New Center Point Road is open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 1:30 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Colorado Springs, CO, 2895 New Center Point Road. - In-N-Out Burger
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM (Sun-Thu) and 1:30 AM (Fri-Sat).

cards.title: The 24-Hour Diner
cards.subtitle: Austin Bluffs Parkway
cards.notes: Visit this 24-hour diner for classic breakfast fare like hashbrowns and waffles at any time of the night.
cards.short_summary: A reliable 24/7 diner chain providing affordable breakfast and comfort food for late-night study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House at 4180 Austin Bluffs Pkwy is a 24-hour location in Colorado Springs.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

cards.title: Underground Late Bites
cards.subtitle: North Tejon Street
cards.notes: Experience this Alice in Wonderland-themed underground restaurant for late-night New American cuisine until 11:00 PM.
cards.short_summary: An upscale, subterranean dining destination in downtown Colorado Springs known for its unique atmosphere and late-night menu.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rabbit Hole is open seven days a week from 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM for late-night bites.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 4:00 PM to 11:00 PM; reservations recommended.

cards.title: Late-Night Coffee House
cards.subtitle: Shove Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Visit this student-run late-night coffee house in the basement of Shove Chapel for a quiet place to study and drink coffee.
cards.short_summary: A unique, late-night coffee house located in the lower level of Shove Memorial Chapel, providing a peaceful environment for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacred Grounds is a late-night coffee house located on the lower level of Shove Memorial Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Typically open during evening and late-night hours during the academic blocks.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, late-night tea houses, and creative hubs where Colorado College students actually spend their time between blocks.

cards.title: Sacred Grounds Tea House
cards.subtitle: Shove Memorial Chapel Lower Level
cards.notes: Visit this student-led, substance-free space for late-night tea and open mic nights. It is a cozy alternative to the library for evening study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A student-run late-night tea house and study space located in the basement of Shove Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Sacred Grounds is a student-led late-night gathering space open from 9pm-12am Wednesday-Saturday, serving as a substance-free venue and study space.
cards.access_notes: Open late night 9 PM to 12 AM, Wednesday through Saturday.

cards.title: The Bean Table
cards.subtitle: Behind McGregor Hall
cards.notes: Head to this bean-shaped outdoor table for a quiet sunset view of Pikes Peak. It is a favorite spot for solo reflection or small group discussions.
cards.short_summary: A signature bean-shaped outdoor table behind McGregor Hall known for its mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ritt Kellogg Table, often called the 'bean table,' is a student-favorite spot behind McGregor Hall for watching sunsets and reflecting.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public campus space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Fourth Floor 'Fishbowl'
cards.subtitle: Charles L. Tutt Library
cards.notes: Grab a seat in the glass-walled rooms on the top floor for panoramic mountain views. These spaces are highly sought after during finals week.
cards.short_summary: High-visibility glass study rooms on the top floor of the library offering expansive views.
cards.evidence_claim: Students favor the 'window rooms' or 'fishbowl' areas in Tutt Library for the views of the mountains and sunsets.
cards.source_title: Charles L. Tutt Library Self-Guided Tour
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary; typically open late for students with card access.

cards.title: Cornerstone Main Space
cards.subtitle: Cornerstone Arts Center
cards.notes: Use this multi-level atrium for informal socializing or catching pop-up student performances. The architecture itself serves as a stage.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, open atrium in the arts center used for studying, socializing, and impromptu events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cornerstone Main Space is used for performances, classes, or informal socializing and features an innovative layout.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; often used for late-night rehearsals.

cards.title: Ritt Kellogg Climbing Gym
cards.subtitle: Adam F. Press Fitness Center Lower Level
cards.notes: Practice bouldering or top-roping at this free student gym. Equipment is provided, making it an easy spot to de-stress between classes.
cards.short_summary: A 3,500 square-foot indoor climbing facility located within the campus fitness center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ritt Kellogg Climbing Gym is a free indoor rock climbing gym for students with equipment provided.
cards.access_notes: Requires active Gold Card for free student access.

cards.title: Worner Arts & Crafts Studios
cards.subtitle: Worner Campus Center
cards.notes: Join a non-graded class in ceramics, fiber arts, or metal. It is a popular creative outlet for students looking to work with their hands.
cards.short_summary: Student-accessible studios for creative projects outside of the formal academic curriculum.
cards.evidence_claim: Worner Campus Center is home to the Arts & Crafts program studios offering classes in ceramics, fiber arts, and metal.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8:30 AM - 8:00 PM; weekend hours vary.

cards.title: Olin Hall Fishbowl
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall of Science
cards.notes: Study in this glass-enclosed space within the science building. It is known for being a quiet, focused environment for STEM students.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet study area in the science building characterized by its glass walls.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'fishbowl' in Olin Hall is listed as a student favorite study spot on campus.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: The Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Outside Shove Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Walk this stone path for a meditative break. It is a quiet outdoor corner often used by students for mindfulness between intense blocks.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor meditative walking path located on the grounds of Shove Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The labyrinth outside Shove Chapel is identified as a quiet corner and spiritual space for the CC community.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Preserve
cards.subtitle: Western Ridge Apartments
cards.notes: Escape the main dining hall for a quiet afternoon study break. This cafe-grocery hybrid is a favorite for its made-to-order specials.
cards.short_summary: A gourmet cafe and grocery space located in the Western Ridge residential area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Preserve is described as a perfect place for a quiet afternoon study break or weekend gathering.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check dining services for specific block break hours.

cards.title: Honnen 3D Arts Studio
cards.subtitle: 30 W. Cache La Poudre St.
cards.notes: Explore this former ice arena now transformed into a vibrant 3D arts hub. It houses sculpture and installation spaces for student projects.
cards.short_summary: A repurposed ice arena that now serves as the primary facility for 3D arts and sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnen Ice Arena was renovated in 2023 to become the home for the college's 3D Arts department.
cards.source_title: From Ice to Art: Honnen Ice Arena Undergoes Transformation
cards.access_notes: Primarily for art students; exhibitions are often open to the campus community.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best spots and activities at Colorado College that don't cost a dime, from world-class art galleries to historic campus landmarks and scenic trails.

cards.entity_name: Colorado Springs Fine Arts Center at Colorado College
cards.title: Explore the FAC Museum
cards.subtitle: 30 W Dale St
cards.notes: Present your CC Gold Card for free admission to the museum galleries. Public visitors can enjoy free entry during First Friday events from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A premier art museum offering free admission to Colorado College students and staff.
cards.evidence_claim: Colorado College faculty, staff, and students receive free museum admission with a valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Museum is closed Sunday through Tuesday. Open Wednesday, Thursday, and Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., and Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.

cards.title: Meditate in Shove Chapel
cards.subtitle: 1010 N Nevada Ave
cards.notes: Visit this historic Norman Romanesque chapel for quiet reflection or study. It is open to the public on weekdays for contemplative use and spiritual practice.
cards.short_summary: A serene, non-denominational spiritual center open for public meditation and quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel is typically open Monday - Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. through the West doors for the public.
cards.access_notes: Public access is generally limited to business hours; students have late-night key card access.

cards.title: Study at Tutt Library
cards.subtitle: 1021 N Cascade Ave
cards.notes: Utilize the library's extensive collections and guest wireless network. Public visitors are welcome to explore the space and use resources until 6:00 PM daily.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering public access to collections and study spaces during the day.
cards.evidence_claim: While CC is private, collections are open to the public; visitors must leave the building by 6:00 PM.
cards.access_notes: Visitors may be asked to show ID and sign in. Public computer access is currently restricted.

cards.title: Run the Tiger Trail
cards.subtitle: Monument Creek
cards.notes: Jog or walk along this well-maintained 12-foot wide path following Monument Creek. It connects the campus to the broader Colorado Springs urban trail system.
cards.short_summary: A popular paved trail for running and walking that borders the western edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tiger Trail along Monument Creek is a tier-one hard-surfaced trail used frequently by the CC community.
cards.source_title: Colorado Springs' Expansive Urban Trail System
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk; accessible via the west side of campus near the athletic fields.

cards.title: Watch a Tiger Soccer Match
cards.subtitle: 44 W Cache La Poudre St
cards.notes: Cheer on the Tigers at this state-of-the-art soccer venue. Admission to home games is free for students and often open to the public without charge.
cards.short_summary: The home field for CC soccer, offering free admission to many athletic events.
cards.evidence_claim: Home soccer games at Stewart Field, such as the season opener, often feature free admission for the community.
cards.source_title: Today@CC - This Week in CC Athletics
cards.access_notes: Street parking is free after 5pm on weekdays and all day on weekends.

cards.title: Take a Historic Walking Tour
cards.subtitle: Starts at Cutler Hall
cards.notes: Follow a self-guided route to see buildings like Palmer Hall and Cutler Hall. These sites are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided tour of the college's most significant and architecturally diverse historic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Colorado College offers a self-guided walking tour of its historic properties for the public.
cards.access_notes: Best viewed between 9 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. to see building exteriors and some public interiors.

cards.entity_name: Seay Library of Music and Art
cards.title: Listen to Music at Seay
cards.subtitle: Packard Hall, Ground Level
cards.notes: Browse over 31,000 items including CDs and LPs. Use the group listening room or study spaces to enjoy one of the largest music collections in the West.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library for music and art research with public-access listening facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Seay Library facilities include a group listening and viewing room and are open to the public.
cards.source_title: Seay Library of Music and Art
cards.access_notes: Located in Packard Hall; check website for current block-specific operating hours.

cards.title: Hang Out at Worner Center
cards.subtitle: 902 N Cascade Ave
cards.notes: The social hub of campus features lounges, the CC Pantry Exchange, and student organization spaces. It's a great spot to meet friends between blocks.
cards.short_summary: The central student union building hosting free events and providing communal social spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Worner Campus Center is the home of Campus Activities and offers various free events and student spaces.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; specific office hours for Campus Activities are 9 am - 5 pm during block periods.

cards.title: Climb at Ritt Kellogg
cards.subtitle: Adam F. Press Fitness Center
cards.notes: Students with a Gold Card can access this 30-foot climbing wall for free. It features top-rope routes and bouldering problems for all skill levels.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus climbing facility offering free access and equipment for Colorado College students.
cards.evidence_claim: Colorado College students have free access to the Adam F. Press Fitness Center, which includes the climbing gym.
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CC Gold Card for entry. Guests may enter for a fee if accompanied by a member.

cards.title: Borrow Outdoor Essentials
cards.subtitle: 931 N Nevada Ave
cards.notes: Get ready for the mountains with free rentals on hiking boots and outdoor clothing. It's the perfect resource for students exploring the Rockies on a budget.
cards.short_summary: A campus facility providing free and low-cost outdoor gear rentals to the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gear House offers free rentals on necessities like clothing and hiking boots for students.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday through Friday, 9 am - 5 pm. Located at the Outdoor Education Center.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Navigate the intense rhythms of the Block Plan with these ten distinct study environments across the Colorado College campus, from high-tech library labs to quiet historic chapels.

cards.title: Summit Reading Room Views
cards.subtitle: Tutt Library Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Head to the top floor for panoramic mountain views. This space remains open until 2:00 AM during the block, offering a quiet atmosphere for late-night focus.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor reading room in Tutt Library known for its expansive views and late-night availability.
cards.evidence_claim: The Inasmuch Foundation Summit Reading Room is located on the fourth floor of Tutt Library and is open until 2:00 AM Monday-Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM on most nights during the block; accessible to students with CC ID.

cards.title: Quiet Contemplation at Shove
cards.subtitle: 1010 N. Nevada Ave
cards.notes: Use the west doors to enter this Norman Romanesque chapel for silent study. Students have key card access for early morning or late-night sessions.
cards.short_summary: A historic non-denominational chapel offering a silent, meditative environment for reading and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Shove Memorial Chapel is open for quiet study, with students having early morning and late-night key card access.
cards.access_notes: Public hours 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM; student key card access available for late nights.

cards.title: Interdisciplinary Social Study
cards.subtitle: Cornerstone Arts Center
cards.notes: Find a spot in this open atrium for informal socializing or collaborative work. The building's layout encourages creative use of its architectural features.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, open atrium in the Cornerstone Arts Center used for informal study and social interaction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cornerstone Main Space is used for performances, classes, or informal socializing.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; check for scheduled performances which may limit access.

cards.title: The Olin Hall Fishbowl
cards.subtitle: Olin Hall of Science
cards.notes: Visit this glass-walled space for a bright, focused environment. It is a long-standing student favorite for science-heavy study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A glass-enclosed study area in Olin Hall popular for its natural light and academic atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'fishbowl' in Olin Hall is listed as a favorite student study spot.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Olin Hall building hours.

cards.title: Art Library Lounge Retreat
cards.subtitle: Packard Hall Room 123
cards.notes: Relax or work on group projects surrounded by art history theses. This lounge also hosts 'Tea and Sympathy' events for the Art Department.
cards.short_summary: A specialized lounge in Packard Hall dedicated to art students but open for general quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art Library Lounge in Packard Hall 123 is a place to relax, study, and work on small group projects.
cards.source_title: Visual Resources Center (VRC) + Art Lounge - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Open during Packard Hall hours; check for departmental event closures.

cards.entity_name: Helen and Arthur E. Johnson GIS Lab
cards.title: Spatial Analysis & Data Viz
cards.subtitle: Tutt Library Second Floor
cards.notes: Access high-end workstations for spatial analysis and data visualization. Ideal for students integrating geographic information into their research.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused lab in Tutt Library supporting spatial analysis and data-driven research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Helen and Arthur E. Johnson GIS Lab supports spatial analysis and data visualization in Tutt Library.
cards.source_title: Tutt Library Self-Guided Tour - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Available during library hours; priority given to GIS-related research.

cards.title: Upstairs Worner Hangout
cards.subtitle: Worner Campus Center
cards.notes: Head upstairs for a more relaxed study environment near dining options. It's a central hub for informal gatherings and social academic work.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located lounge area in the campus center suitable for casual study and group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Upstairs Worner is identified as a favorite student study spot.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8:30 AM - 8:00 PM, weekends 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Collaborative Group Rooms
cards.subtitle: Tutt Library Multiple Floors
cards.notes: Reserve a room using the digital panels outside or via webmail. Groups of three or more have priority for these high-demand collaborative spaces.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms throughout Tutt Library equipped with screens for group projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Tutt Library offers group study rooms that can be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required; 2-hour limit; groups of 3+ have priority.

cards.title: Light-Filled Honnen Study
cards.subtitle: Honnen Arts Building
cards.notes: Study in a high-vaulted, light-filled classroom in the restored Honnen building. Afternoon access is often available when events are not scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A bright, modern classroom space in the former ice arena, now dedicated to creativity and innovation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Honnen building features a high-vaulted, light-filled classroom used for classes and events.
cards.access_notes: Mornings reserved for classes; check availability for afternoon study use.

cards.title: Senior Thesis Carrels
cards.subtitle: Tutt Library Second Floor
cards.notes: Fourth-year students can reserve these dedicated carrels by the block. It provides a consistent, private space for long-term thesis research.
cards.short_summary: Reserved study carrels in Tutt Library specifically for seniors working on their thesis projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Quon Corner Study Carrels can be reserved by fourth-year students by the block.
cards.source_title: Tutt Library Self-Guided Tour - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Reservation restricted to seniors; general seating nearby for other students.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the streets and corridors surrounding Colorado College, from the historic Old North End to the bustling downtown Tejon Street district.

cards.title: Poor Richard's
cards.subtitle: North Tejon Street
cards.notes: Browse used books and grab a slice of solar-baked pizza at this local landmark founded by a CC alumnus. It serves as a community living room just blocks from campus.
cards.short_summary: A multi-concept bookstore and pizzeria on the Tejon Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Poor Richard's was started in 1975 by Colorado College senior Richard Skorman and remains a downtown landmark and student favorite.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for dining and browsing; located on the 300 block of North Tejon Street.

cards.title: Old North End
cards.subtitle: North Cascade Avenue
cards.notes: Walk through this historic district featuring Victorian mansions and tree-lined medians. It is a popular residential area for students and faculty north of campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential neighborhood adjacent to the northern edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old North End is a historic neighborhood north of downtown where students walk to and from class on the Colorado College campus.
cards.source_title: Old North End & Surrounding Communities - Visit Colorado Springs
cards.access_notes: Public residential neighborhood accessible for walking and biking at all times.

cards.title: Uintah Gardens
cards.subtitle: West Uintah Street
cards.notes: Visit this shopping center for grocery runs and essentials. It is a primary commercial hub for students living on the west side of the campus corridor.
cards.short_summary: A shopping center located less than two miles west of the college campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Uintah Gardens Shopping Center features a King Soopers and other retail shops frequently used by the Colorado College community.
cards.source_title: SUV Crashes into King Soopers on Uintah Street - The Catalyst
cards.access_notes: Commercial center with standard retail hours; King Soopers typically open until late evening.

cards.title: Josh & John's
cards.subtitle: East Pikes Peak Avenue
cards.notes: Enjoy slow-churned ice cream at this downtown staple founded by a CC alum. Try the Purple Mountain Majesty flavor while exploring the downtown core.
cards.short_summary: An iconic ice cream shop founded by a Colorado College graduate.
cards.evidence_claim: Josh & John's was founded in 1986 by CC alum John Krakauer and is a recognized institution in downtown Colorado Springs.
cards.source_title: One Scoop at a Time - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Open daily for walk-in service; located near the intersection of Tejon and Pikes Peak.

cards.title: Pikes Peak Greenway
cards.subtitle: Monument Creek Trail
cards.notes: Run or bike along the Tiger Trail section of this urban path. It follows Monument Creek directly behind the campus athletic fields.
cards.short_summary: A major urban trail system running along the western edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pikes Peak Greenway, also known as the Tiger Trail, runs along Monument Creek behind the Colorado College campus.
cards.source_title: Colorado Springs' Expansive Urban Trail System - The Catalyst
cards.access_notes: Public trail open for recreation from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: East Campus Housing
cards.subtitle: North Weber Street
cards.notes: Walk past the college-owned theme houses and apartments that line this street. It serves as the primary residential corridor for upper-division students.
cards.short_summary: A residential street featuring Colorado College student housing and theme houses.
cards.evidence_claim: Weber Street contains several Colorado College residential properties, including 1018 N Weber, which is part of the East Campus Housing Community.
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require student ID for entry.

cards.title: Loyal Coffee
cards.subtitle: North Nevada Avenue
cards.notes: Study with a specialty latte at this barista-built cafe. The downtown location on Nevada is a popular off-campus workspace for students and faculty.
cards.short_summary: A specialty coffee shop and popular study spot on the Nevada Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyal Coffee's downtown location is a popular coffee shop for Colorado College professors and students alike.
cards.source_title: Our Favorite Colorado Springs Coffee Shops for Studying
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 6 AM to 6 PM.

cards.title: Shooks Run Trail
cards.subtitle: East of Campus
cards.notes: Explore this 4-mile paved trail that connects historic neighborhoods east of campus. It offers a scenic route for biking and walking through local parks.
cards.short_summary: An urban trail and greenway located a few blocks east of the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Shooks Run Trail is a central Colorado Springs urban trail that follows Shooks Run Creek through historic neighborhoods near the college.
cards.source_title: Shooks Run Trail - Trails & Open Space Coalition
cards.access_notes: Public trail accessible daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Stir Coffee & Cocktails
cards.subtitle: North Wahsatch Avenue
cards.notes: Visit this literary-themed cafe for a quiet study session or a seasonal quiche. It is located just north of campus in the Old North End neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood cafe and bar with a library-inspired atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: STIR sits just north of the Colorado College campus and is described as a perfect place for students to work or relax.
cards.source_title: ON TAP: STIR it Up - The Catalyst
cards.access_notes: Open daily; coffee service starts at 9 AM. Under-21 safe for cafe use.

cards.title: Fine Arts Center
cards.subtitle: West Dale Street
cards.notes: Visit the museum galleries or attend a theatre production at this multidisciplinary arts institution. It marks the southwestern edge of the campus corridor.
cards.short_summary: A major museum and performing arts center integrated with the college.
cards.evidence_claim: The Colorado Springs Fine Arts Center at Colorado College is located at 30 W. Dale St. and serves as a museum, theatre, and art school.
cards.source_title: About the FAC - Fine Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Museum galleries open Wednesday-Sunday; CC students receive free admission with ID.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the Colorado College experience, from the intensity of the Block Plan to the creative energy of student-run festivals.

cards.title: The Block Plan
cards.subtitle: One Course at a Time
cards.notes: Immerse yourself in a single subject for three and a half weeks. This intensive academic structure has defined the CC experience since its adoption in 1970.
cards.short_summary: Colorado College's signature academic calendar where students take one class at a time for 3.5 weeks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block Plan was officially unveiled in 1969 and implemented in 1970 to solve the 'crisis of time' in student life.
cards.source_title: The Story of the Block Plan
cards.access_notes: The primary academic schedule for all undergraduate students.

cards.title: Block Break
cards.subtitle: The 4.5-Day Recharge
cards.notes: After every block, enjoy a four-and-a-half-day break starting Wednesday at noon. It is the essential time for students to recharge before the next intensive course.
cards.short_summary: A recurring 4.5-day break between academic blocks used for rest, travel, or outdoor adventure.
cards.evidence_claim: Block breaks begin at noon on the fourth Wednesday of every block and last until the following Monday.
cards.access_notes: Occurs eight times per academic year following the conclusion of each block.

cards.title: Llamapalooza
cards.subtitle: Annual Music & Arts Festival
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the academic year at this student-run festival featuring live bands, DJs, and art. It is a cornerstone of the Block 8 social calendar.
cards.short_summary: A major annual music and arts festival held on campus during the final block of the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Llamapalooza is CC's annual music and arts festival, typically held during Block 8 and featuring both student and outside performers.
cards.access_notes: Held annually on the quad; open to the campus community.

cards.title: Midnight Rasty
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Breakfast Oasis
cards.notes: Head to Rastall Dining Hall for a late-night feast of pancakes and tater tots. This tradition provides a safe, social space during high-energy campus weekends.
cards.short_summary: A late-night breakfast event held at Rastall Dining Hall during major campus weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Rasty (or Midnight Breakfast) is a campus-sponsored event at Rastall Dining Hall that serves up to 1,300 students during events like Winter Ball.
cards.source_title: Late-Night Oasis: The Life Behind Midnight Rasty
cards.access_notes: Typically held from midnight to 2:00 AM during specific blocks or major events.

cards.title: Dance Workshop
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Performance
cards.notes: Watch or join over 250 students in this massive, student-run production. It features original choreography from dancers of all experience levels twice a year.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale, biannual student-run dance production involving hundreds of campus participants.
cards.evidence_claim: Dance Workshop has been a CC tradition since 1986, involving over 250 student dancers and choreographers in Blocks 4 and 7.
cards.access_notes: Performances are held in the Armstrong Hall theater or similar campus venues.

cards.title: First Mondays
cards.subtitle: Community Intellectual Life
cards.notes: Gather with the entire campus on the first Monday of each block for a keynote lecture. Classes end early to ensure everyone can participate in the discussion.
cards.short_summary: A monthly campus-wide event featuring lectures and discussions to kick off each new academic block.
cards.evidence_claim: On the first Monday of each block, classes release early to allow the community to attend First Mondays talks.
cards.access_notes: Held midday on the first Monday of Blocks 2 through 7.

cards.title: The Honor Code
cards.subtitle: A Tradition of Trust
cards.notes: Sign the pledge on every assignment to uphold academic integrity. This student-run system has been a pillar of the college's culture of mutual trust since 1948.
cards.short_summary: A student-enforced academic integrity system established in 1948 based on mutual trust.
cards.evidence_claim: The Colorado College Honor System was established in 1948 and requires students to sign a pledge on all written work.
cards.access_notes: Applies to all academic work completed for credit at the college.

cards.title: Tiger Trail
cards.subtitle: The Walk to Stewart Field
cards.notes: Walk the path down McGregor Hill to Stewart Field, passing the tiger head sculpture. It features an 1898 motivational quote from President William F. Slocum.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped walkway connecting the main campus to the athletic fields, featuring historic quotes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tiger Trail is marked at the top with a tiger head sculpture and an engraved 1898 quote from President Slocum.
cards.source_title: Tiger Trail Walkway to Stewart Field
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public walkway accessible at all times.

cards.title: Aspen Bike Trip
cards.subtitle: Longest Running Block Break
cards.notes: Join the annual 160-mile cycling journey to Aspen during a fall block break. It is celebrated as the college's longest-running annual block break tradition.
cards.short_summary: A traditional 160-mile group bicycle ride from campus to Aspen held during a fall block break.
cards.evidence_claim: The Aspen bike trip is described as the longest running annual block break tradition, featuring a 160-mile ride.
cards.access_notes: Typically organized through the Outdoor Education department during a fall block break.

cards.title: Winter Ball
cards.subtitle: Formal Campus Celebration
cards.notes: Dress up for the college's premier formal event of the winter season. It is a major social tradition that brings the entire student body together for a night of dancing.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing formal dance event held annually during the winter months.
cards.evidence_claim: Winter Ball is identified as one of the favorite and most widely attended campus-sponsored traditions at Colorado College.
cards.source_title: Bringing the CC Community Together: Practicing CC Traditions
cards.access_notes: Held annually; location varies but often on campus or at the Fine Arts Center.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Colorado College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Kick Off at NSO Check-In
cards.subtitle: Pick up your Gold Card and keys
cards.notes: Start your weekend by heading to the arena to collect your student ID, room keys, and orientation materials. This is the official first stop for all new Tigers.
cards.short_summary: The primary check-in hub for New Student Orientation (NSO) and move-in logistics.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student move-in and NSO check-in take place at Ed Robson Arena starting at 8:00 am on move-in Monday.
cards.access_notes: Open for check-in from 8:00 am to 12:00 pm on designated move-in days.

cards.title: Welcome Lunch on the Grass
cards.subtitle: Refuel with fellow new families
cards.notes: After moving into your dorm, walk over to the central quad for a relaxed outdoor lunch under the orientation tents. It is a great spot to meet your first few classmates.
cards.short_summary: The central campus green space used for major orientation gatherings and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: A Welcome Lunch is held on Tava Quad from 11:00 am to 1:00 pm following morning move-in.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space; lunch event specifically for new students and families.

cards.title: Dinner at 'Rasty'
cards.subtitle: Experience the community hub
cards.notes: Swipe your Gold Card for an all-you-care-to-eat dinner. Visit the stir-fry station or the pizza oven while meeting people in the college's main social dining space.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus dining facility located within the Worner Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Rastall Dining Hall is the main cafeteria where students swipe their Gold Card for meals, featuring multiple food stations.
cards.access_notes: Standard dinner hours are 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm; requires a meal plan swipe or payment.

cards.title: Explore with your Priddy Group
cards.subtitle: Local service and exploration
cards.notes: Join your small group of 10-12 peers for a half-day of community service or a local hike. This tradition helps you bond with your first CC 'family.'
cards.short_summary: A signature orientation program involving small-group service and outdoor activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Priddy Experience involves small groups participating in service, local, and outdoor programs during orientation week.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Education - Priddy Experience - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Required for all new students; locations vary by group assignment.

cards.title: Hike the Red Rocks
cards.subtitle: Iconic Colorado Springs scenery
cards.notes: Take a short 10-minute drive or a college shuttle to see the massive sandstone formations. It is the quintessential first-weekend outdoor excursion for CC students.
cards.short_summary: A public park featuring dramatic red rock formations and numerous hiking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Garden of the Gods is a 10-minute drive from campus and is a frequent destination for student field trips and recreation.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 5:00 am to 9:00 pm; free admission to the park.

cards.title: Get Creative at Worner
cards.subtitle: Late-night making and DIY
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of Worner to try your hand at ceramics or fiber arts. It is a low-pressure way to spend a Friday afternoon or evening with new friends.
cards.short_summary: A co-curricular studio space offering non-graded art-making opportunities for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arts and Crafts Studio is located in the lower level of Worner Campus Center and offers classes and open studio time.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday until 7:30 pm, Fridays until 5:00 pm, and Sundays 2:00 pm-5:00 pm.

cards.title: Late Night at the Rink
cards.subtitle: Themed skating at Robson Arena
cards.notes: Check the weekend digest for themed skate nights. It is a popular late-night activity where you can rent skates and hit the ice with the campus community.
cards.short_summary: Periodic themed ice skating events held at the campus hockey arena.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Night Skates are coordinated by Campus Activities at Robson Arena, typically on Friday or Saturday nights.
cards.access_notes: Occurs periodically; check the OCA Instagram or Weekend Digest for specific dates and times.

cards.title: Art Break at the FAC
cards.subtitle: Free museum access for students
cards.notes: Show your student ID for free entry to the museum galleries. It is a quiet, air-conditioned escape just a block away from the main campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A major regional art museum and theatre that is a division of Colorado College.
cards.evidence_claim: Colorado College students receive free museum admission to the Fine Arts Center with their student ID.
cards.source_title: Tickets – Fine Arts Center - Colorado College
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00 am to 5:00 pm.

cards.title: Find Your Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Late-night prep for Block 1
cards.notes: Explore the four floors of the library to find your favorite spot before classes start. The fourth floor stays open late for those who need a quiet workspace.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library, designed to support the intensive pace of the Block Plan.
cards.evidence_claim: Tutt Library offers regular block hours until 12:00 am, with the fourth floor remaining open until 2:00 am.
cards.access_notes: Gold Card required for entry after 6:00 pm; 4th floor open until 2:00 am during blocks.

cards.title: Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: The official start of the year
cards.notes: Gather with the entire campus community on Monday morning to officially kick off the academic year. It is a formal tradition that marks the end of your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A historic Norman Romanesque chapel used for major college ceremonies and traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Opening Convocation is a CC tradition held in Shove Memorial Chapel to welcome new students and kick off the academic year.
cards.source_title: Join Us for Opening Convocation on Monday, Aug. 24 - Today@CC
cards.access_notes: Event typically starts at 9:00 am on the first Monday of Block 1.
